name: Thymic Epithelial Neoplasm

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Thymic Epithelial Tumors

criteria.description: Histological confirmation of thymic epithelial tumor subtype
CT or MRI showing anterior mediastinal mass consistent with thymic tumor
Presence of paraneoplastic syndromes such as myasthenia gravis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation combined with imaging evidence of an anterior mediastinal mass
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of metastatic disease and other mediastinal masses

pathognomonic.symptomName: Anterior mediastinal mass detected on imaging
searchTerms: mass in front of chest detected by scan

pathognomonic.symptomName: Myasthenia gravis with fluctuating skeletal muscle weakness
pathognomonic.notes: Common paraneoplastic syndrome associated with thymoma
searchTerms: weakness in skeletal muscles varying over time

common.symptomName: Chest pain localized to anterior mediastinum
common.notes: Due to tumor invasion or compression
searchTerms: chest pain in front of chest

common.notes: From mass effect or pleural effusion
Compression of superior vena cava by tumor

occasional.symptomName: Hoarseness due to recurrent laryngeal nerve involvement
searchTerms: hoarse voice due to nerve involvement
unintentional weight loss and poor appetite
low red blood cells from chronic illness
chronic disease causing low blood count
failure to produce red blood cells
pure red cell aplasia causing anemia

rare.symptomName: Superior mediastinal syndrome with facial edema
searchTerms: swelling of face from upper chest vein blockage
facial edema due to mediastinal compression
superior mediastinal syndrome with facial swelling

laboratory: Elevated acetylcholine receptor antibodies in myasthenia gravis
Anemia or cytopenias in paraneoplastic syndromes
imaging: CT scan showing well-defined anterior mediastinal mass
PET scan for metabolic activity and staging
genetic: Somatic mutations occasionally found in thymic carcinoma subtypes

redFlags: Signs of superior vena cava syndrome
New onset or worsening myasthenic crisis
references: Travis WD, Brambilla E, Burke AP, Marx A, Nicholson AG. WHO Classification of Tumours of the Lung, Pleura, Thymus and Heart. IARC; 2015.
Detterbeck FC, Zeeshan A. Thymoma: current diagnosis and treatment. Chin J Cancer Res. 2013;25(1):19-29.
Engels EA. Epidemiology of thymoma and associated malignancies. J Thorac Oncol. 2010;5(10 Suppl 4):S260-5.
